newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Analysts say Serbia employer tax relief not enough.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say Serbia employer tax relief not enough.

text.p: The Serbian parliament cut employers' tax burden on Wednesday, but analysts said the fiscal adjustment would not substantially relieve the country's cash-starved economy.

The government said the cut in employers' social security contributions to 21 from the present 25 percent would free some 350 million dinars by the end of the year to be redirected into boosting production.
Large cash-strapped companies have called on the government to reduce the burden on employers of the wages-tax ratio from the current 1-1.2 to 1-1.
Economists saw the fiscal cut as a positive step but said it would raise the question of financing pensions, especially the health fund, which is on the brink of collapse.

"Although the cuts are necessary, they are absolutely not enough. It is just transferring the tax burden from employers to the impoverished population," Aleksandra Posarac of the Institute of Economic Sciences told Reuters.
The new rate, valid from October 1, is seen cutting inflow into social funds by around 180 million dinars by year end.
The government said the deficit would be covered by raising taxes on tobacco and postal and telephone rates and stricter tax discipline.
The republican parliament also passed a draft law on labour relations obliging each company or store to have a minimum of two employees.
The move is expected to raise the number of tax payers by around 200,000 since most private companies and stores do not register their employees to avoid paying taxes.
"The real solution lies in cutting budget expenditures since they are exerting inflationary and recessionary pressure on the economy," Posarac said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
